method: Selected passages inspected through web document extraction. This is not human verification. Passage locators use printed page numbers for PDFs.

sources.title: Walkerton Inquiry, Part One: A Summary (2002), official report reproduced by the Water Supply Association of B.C.
sources.supports: Printed pp. 2–4, 9–10 and 31–33: toll, Well 5, farm practices, adverse results, disclosure and notification requirements.
claimEvidence: Well 5 and farm-practice finding; later toll; concealed results; absent binding notification

sources.title: Bruce-Grey-Owen Sound Health Unit and Health Canada, Waterborne Outbreak of Gastroenteritis, CCDR 26-20 (October 15, 2000)
sources.supports: Printed pp. 170–171: epidemiologic investigation, advisory, reported versus estimated case totals and contemporary death count.
claimEvidence: Advisory timestamp; reported/estimated distinction; six deaths in this dated report

sources.title: Clark and colleagues, Characterization of Waterborne Outbreak–associated Campylobacter jejuni, Walkerton, Ontario (2003)
sources.supports: Environmental Specimens, Results and Discussion: sampling dates, 57 water samples, typing evidence and limits of attribution.
inspectedPassages: Environmental Specimens; Results opening paragraphs; Discussion paragraphs 1–5 and molecular-surveillance caveat
claimEvidence: Delayed farm sampling; two principal strain groups; 57 negative water samples; qualified source attribution

sources.title: Health Canada, Guidance on waterborne pathogens in drinking water
sources.supports: Sections A.3.2–A.3.3: treatment, concentration and contact time, multiple operating parameters, training and distribution-system risks.
inspectedPassages: A.3.2 Water treatment plant, numbered operating elements
A.3.3 Drinking water distribution system, entry mechanisms and operating practices
claimEvidence: Disinfection exposure and process monitoring; training; downstream entry and controls

limitations: Ontario archive URLs inspected during discovery now redirect to an archive landing page; the reproduced government report is transparently identified as a mirror.
The full inquiry was not reviewed; no claim is made of exhaustive archival coverage.
No explanation for the six-versus-seven death-count difference was established from inspected passages.
No causal percentages, present-day compliance judgment or individual medical advice is offered.

rights.sourceSummaryPolicy: Body uses compact paraphrases from four independent documents; evidence locators avoid reproducing source passages.
